analysis: Extended ensemble analysis: weighted-average grid search + logistic-regression stacking, on fresh seeded models (127/23 split)
key_finding: Two independent ensemble strategies were tested. Weighted-average grid search assigned 100% weight to Fusion-MIL, giving no improvement (0.9538 unchanged). Logistic-regression stacking performed WORSE than Fusion-MIL alone (0.8846 vs 0.9538) -- the meta-learner's positive coefficients on the weaker CNN-MIL and Foundation-MIL predictions diluted Fusion-MIL's stronger, more confident predictions. This is consistent, cross-method evidence that ensembling does not help in this setup: Fusion-MIL already internally combines CNN and foundation-model signal, leaving no complementary information for an external ensemble (of either kind) to exploit.
caveat: Both ensemble methods were fit AND evaluated on the same 23-slide validation set (no separate ensemble-validation split), which is optimistic/circular by construction, especially for the stacking method with 3 learnable parameters on n=23. The comparative finding (stacking underperforms weighted-average, both underperform or match the single best model) is more trustworthy than any individual AUROC number here.
